local_checks.invariant: Program rename/merge and run moves authorised and atomic
local_checks.result: program_rename admin_required with confirm+reason, one transaction; move_run atomic; run_tag requires can_open for a new program and a registered key; owner/workbook changes admin-only. Gap covered by the candidate: week_start edits skip can_open when program is unchanged.

local_checks.invariant: Independent verification of candidate runs.uploader-access-outlives-program-removal
local_checks.result: Verdict needs_validation; trace verified=True; preventing control found=False. app.py:445-446 returns True for the uploader before any can_open check. _run_or_404 (runs.py:54) and _version_or_404 (schedule_versions.py:37) rely on it; the wall (app.py:394-401) is skipped for path-id routes (no 'program' value). _may_set_in_use and _may_delete (schedule_versions.py:41-48) test only admin or uploader. set_user_programs (store.py:679) does not reassign or revoke the user's runs,

hardening_notes: RunQueue.stop() QUEUED branch writes STOPPED without self._lock while _claim() can have moved the run to GATE; the worker keeps executing and a later Resume could start a second execution of the same results folder when PARALLEL>1. Do the check and update under the lock, conditional on status='QUEUED'.
resume() and run_delete have check-then-act status reads without a lock or conditional update.
stop and resume need only visibility plus 'runs', while zone/tag/delete/set-in-use need uploader or admin; confirm any same-program planner may stop or resume a colleague's run.

submit() runs the workbook check synchronously (up to 300 s) on 8 waitress threads; no per-user or global limit on queued or stored runs (30-day retention): a user with 'runs' can occupy request threads or fill disk. Add a per-user in-flight cap and move the check into the worker.
run_tag/apply_run_change compute the preview and apply in separate steps (same-principal TOCTOU only).
RUN_ID uses ^...$ which also matches a trailing newline; harmless today (exact DB lookup follows); use re.fullmatch or \Z.
cleanup() rmtree after a stale list_runs snapshot can race a Resume of an old STOPPED or FAILED run; re-read status under the lock.
Access.__init__ runs ProgramBook.sync() (a write) on every request that builds Access; harmless registry registration, but a read path doing writes.

local_checks.invariant: Break-change and coaching requests cannot create approval from a lower principal or cross program
local_checks.result: Program and permission enforced in route; update_change_request has no status compare-and-swap, so concurrent decide/cancel/expire can overwrite terminal status (same principals, hardening).

local_checks.invariant: Migrations and delete_user fail closed with constant identifiers
local_checks.result: Held: literal ALTER/pragma names; delete_user zeroes roles/programs, randomises hash, cancels open requests.

hardening_notes: store.authenticate failed-login counter is a non-atomic read-modify-write (same issue as candidate h1-lockout-counter-lost-update).

swaps.answer checks only roster_name == row['other'], not that the answering user can open row['program']. Roster-name uniqueness is enforced only among users sharing a program, so a namesake associate in another program could accept a swap meant for someone else; the TM approval step still follows. Fix: also require can_open(row['program']) and that the account is the one swaps.account(program, other) resolves to.

swaps: a failed _apply after both sides were TM-approved returns status to waiting_tm with tm_a_id and tm_b_id still set; _mine then returns [] for every approver so nobody can approve or refuse. A swap left 'applying' by a crash has no recover() (unlike leave.recover()), cannot be cancelled and blocks both days through _open_days. Fix: clear tm ids on rollback; add swaps recover() at start-up.
change_requests: update_change_request has no status guard; use 'update ... where id=? and status=waiting' so concurrent cancel/expire/decide cannot overwrite a terminal state.

Two admins acting concurrently (A disables or demotes B while B does the same to A) can leave zero active admins; recovery needs manage.py enable-user. Check the last-admin count inside one begin immediate transaction in set_active and update_user.

admin_user_action does not reject a deleted target (get_user returns deleted rows): an admin or an all-programs supervisor can enable or reset the password of a 'deleted-N' account, which then signs in as a role-less planner with no programs. No data access gained. Fix: 404 when target['deleted'].

add_user: usernames of the form deleted-<id> are not reserved, so a manager can create one that makes a later delete_user for that id raise IntegrityError. Self-inflicted availability only. Reserve the prefix in username_problem.

Store._db wraps reads and writes without begin immediate except in transaction(); multi-step check-then-act flows (leave.ask overlap check, add_user username check) rely on the unique constraint or the in-process day lock. Low impact, same principal.

local_checks.invariant: Every POST carries CSRF token; authenticated routes pass login_required incl. must_change/expiry wall
local_checks.result: check_csrf first in before_request (compare_digest, ASCII guard); scripted scan of every @app.route found only login, logout, set_theme undecorated (intended). No bypass.

local_checks.invariant: Session lifecycle: fixation, logout revocation, password change/reset invalidation, disable/delete
local_checks.result: Login session.clear() then fresh csrf; load_user rejects inactive users, changed pw stamp, revoked (user_id, at), at < sessions_from; no absolute cap (known).

local_checks.invariant: Post-login redirect cannot leave the site
local_checks.result: SAFE_NEXT fullmatch: leading slash, no second slash/backslash/control/space; login_required re-passes next through safe_next. No open redirect.

local_checks.invariant: IP throttle key not client-chosen behind Caddy (ProxyFix x_for=1)
local_checks.result: Waitress on 127.0.0.1; ProxyFix trusts last XFF entry written by Caddy; remote_addr only address use. No client evasion source-visible; depends on Caddy config (hardening).

local_checks.invariant: After 5 wrong passwords an account locks even under concurrency
local_checks.result: authenticate reads failed, runs scrypt, writes failed+1 absolute, own connection, no begin immediate; 8 Waitress threads can overwrite each other. Candidate h1-lockout-counter-lost-update (needs_validation).

local_checks.invariant: Unknown, locked and known accounts indistinguishable by message and work
local_checks.result: Messages uniform; dummy scrypt equalises one hash, but a known unlocked account with a padded password is hashed twice (typed then cleaned) vs once for unknown/locked. Candidate h1-login-timing-padded-password-enumeration (needs_validation).

local_checks.invariant: Independent verification of candidate h1-lockout-counter-lost-update
local_checks.result: Verdict needs_validation; trace verified=True; preventing control found=False. authenticate (store.py:948-973) is read-verify-write on a private connection with no begin immediate (952-967) and no in-process lock; the only sign-in locks are in throttle.py. Waitress runs 8 threads and scrypt sits between read (953) and absolute write (965), so concurrent wrong guesses can share a stale counter and a stale write can zero locked_until. hardening_notes: Throttle.held/failed protect addresses as seen by ProxyFix(x_for=1): correct while Caddy overwrites or appends X-Forwarded-For (no trusted_proxies). Pin that in deploy docs; do not widen x_for.
SignInThrottle.failed scans every tracked address on each failure (O(n)); rotating many source addresses (e.g. IPv6 /64) grows the dict and CPU per failed login. Availability-class.
Per-IP throttle holds a whole address including right passwords; users on one NAT lose sign-in 15 min after 40 wrong tries. Accepted by design.
Per-account lock at 5 wrong passwords is an accepted lockout-denial lever (admin unlock exists); not re-reported.
logout revocation entries pruned after 30 days, past the 1-hour lifetime: no replay window.

No default-deny global login gate: authentication is per-route via decorators; scan found no unprotected non-public route today, but a new route without a decorator would be open (consider an endpoint allow-list check in before_request).

local_checks.invariant: Every route has a role gate and a program gate bound to the program the handler acts on
local_checks.result: Enumerated all 135 routes against ENDPOINTS: role gate holds. Central program gate (app.py:394-401) reads request.values (args first) but most /day/* POST handlers read request.form['program'] and never re-check can_open (only day_absences and day_operating_start do). Candidate day.post.program.gate-source-mismatch. Path-id routes go through _run_or_404/_version_or_404.

local_checks.invariant: People-permission holder manages only users within own program scope
local_checks.result: can_manage (access.py:59-71) uses shared-program intersection, not containment; reset shows a temporary password to the manager. Candidate people.can_manage.partial-overlap-takeover.

local_checks.invariant: Leave, swap, break-change approvals bind role, program, team manager; cancel binds ownership
local_checks.result: Decide paths enforce permission plus may_approve_for plus can_open(row.program); cancel checks requester id. Two minor gaps raised as candidates: swaps.answer matches only roster_name; requests_coaching_cancel redirects with arbitrary request's program.
